title: Residue-field power-series presentation of an equicharacteristic complete local ring
statement: Let $(C,\mathfrak n)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and suppose there is a unital ring map from a field $k$ to $C$. Put $F=C/\mathfrak n$ and let $\rho:C\to F$ be the quotient map. For every integer $r\ge0$ and every tuple $y_1,\ldots,y_r\in\mathfrak n$ generating $\mathfrak n$, there exist unital ring homomorphisms $\alpha:F\to C$ and $\psi:Q=F[[z_1,\ldots,z_r]]\to C$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] such that $\rho\alpha=\operatorname{id}_F$, $\psi$ restricts on constants to $\alpha$, $\psi(z_i)=y_i$, $\psi$ is surjective, and $\ker\psi\subseteq\mathfrak l=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$. Moreover $Q$ is a Noetherian complete regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] with maximal ideal $\mathfrak l$. No compatibility between $\alpha$ and the original map from $k$ is asserted.

proof.text: Let $p\ge0$ be the characteristic of $F$. The composite $k\to C\xrightarrow{\rho}F$ is unital and hence injective: a nonzero element in its kernel would have an inverse and force $1_F=0$. Thus $k$ has characteristic $p$, and $p\cdot1_C=0$ (also for $p=0$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists] to the complete local ring $C$, obtaining $\Lambda\subseteq C$ with $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak n=p\Lambda$ and residue isomorphism $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak n)\simeq F$. Since $p\cdot1_C=0$, it is zero in the subring $\Lambda$, so $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak n=0$. The residue isomorphism therefore identifies $\Lambda$ itself with $F$. Compose its inverse with $\Lambda\hookrightarrow C$ to obtain a unital map $\alpha:F\to C$ satisfying $\rho\alpha=\operatorname{id}_F$. Nothing chooses this section relative to $k$.

Apply [lem-trf-coefficient-field-generator-presentation] with its field $F=C/\mathfrak n$, ring $R=C$, residue-field isomorphism the identity, coefficient section $\sigma=\alpha$, and the given tuple $y_1,\ldots,y_r$. The Noetherianity, completeness, section identity and generator conditions are precisely the hypotheses already in force. Its surjection $\Phi$, after renaming $T_i$ as $z_i$, is the required $\psi:Q\to C$ with the prescribed constants and variables. It also gives $\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak l$, whence $\ker\psi\subseteq\mathfrak l$ because $0\in\mathfrak n$. For $r=0$ the generator condition says $\mathfrak n=0$; then $Q=F$ and $\psi=\alpha$ is inverse to $\rho$, so its kernel is zero.

proof.text: Apply the field case of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] to the field $F$ and $d=r$. Its clauses (1), (3) and (4) give that $Q=F[[z_1,\ldots,z_r]]$ is Noetherian, local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak l=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$, complete for that ideal, and regular local. This includes $r=0$, when $Q=F$ has maximal ideal zero and dimension zero.

The map from k to F is injective, so char k = p and p·1_C = 0. Then Λ∩n = pΛ = 0, so Λ ≅ F and the section α follows. This is correct and is where the field k is used. The char-0-only residue-section node does not cover it. Step 2 cites lem-trf-coefficient-field-generator-presentation (same unit, no cycle) with ρ = id and σ = α. Cases tested: r=0; F[ε]/(ε²) with kernel (z²) ⊆ (z); zero or redundant generators; imperfect residue field in char p; mixed characteristic is excluded by the field hypothesis. Duplicate candidates read: the pbc Cohen presentation and surjection nodes and the complete-local-map Cohen presentation node. All of them give a Cohen ring in residue char p, not a coefficient field with prescribed generators, so there is no duplicate. I accept the two generic pbc tool_uses (032A(1) and 032C).
